comments.body: Because there are thousands of games, most of which are not particularly good, the algorithm needs to show lots of people lots of garbage to learn what is and is not garbage ("what are players reacting positively to right now?" is the big question); if someone sees only garbage, they will disengage from the process and not discover the actual good games. comments.author: SakuraKoiMaji
comments.body:
A tale as old as time. Or at least as old as the RPG Maker.

Accessibility is very much important in one way and in another way it is important to not overhype. Most 14 year olds will just make and release trash games but it was a great leap that they even can do that. Key is constructive criticism which can range from advice to indeed shaming. 

Shaming however is supposed to be reserved for arrogance and shamelessness, not 'this is my first game I worked on while learning many systems and I wanted to share it'. Yeah, the teen likely sucked at everything, be it story, characters, map design, puzzles but as long as they don't say 'this game is great', one shouldn't say 'this game is trash'. The question should be 'would you like some advice? and on what to start with?'.

The danger for already experienced and professional devs is when managers just demand the use of AI to cut time and costs. Since devs still have to try, learn and experiment, how dare managers dare to know that AI can just do anything and better so?

comments.author: JefersonTomazella
comments.body:
>people who can't code become "more effective developers of value" than [those who've been coding for a decade](https://www.pcgamer.com/software/ai/gabe-newell-reckons-ai-tools-will-result-in-a-funny-situation-where-people-who-cant-program-become-more-effective-developers-of-value-than-those-whove-been-at-it-for-a-decade/). - Gabe

That's so true. People get so used to do the same thing, the same way, that a change in perspective is seems as a dangerous threat.

I am a developer for more than a decade, and AI just helped me do really better stuff, really faster, and I'm still doing the things! I have the ideas, not the AI. 

When I first coded something, in 2003, while learning the Pascal coding language, I made a simple command line game that made my mind explode "I CAN DO THINGS!".

Now I got that same feeling, but making games and tools that actually are useful and fun! And in less time than I made that first game!

We can create our dream projects even with like 1 hour per day, or less. I can take care of my son while I'm making games. How incredible is that?

comments.author: EchoLocation8
comments.body:
For me it’s about how AI was used.  Because, as a software engineer, having Claude build a cloud formation template for me…is my AWS environment “made with AI”?  I told it what to do, what services to use, how it needs to function, all Claude did was type faster than I can type.

Like, trying to take the moral ground that any AI use would dissuade you from using some software (games included), you’d have to stop using everything.  Now, I’m not cool with using it to generate art assets or generate stories or that sort of thing, but code?  Programming has always been predicated on being unoriginal, that’s why open source libraries exist, it’s always been about stealing or using other people’s code.  You try to be unoriginal, you use publicly published design patterns.  Before Claude you’d google and pull things from stack overflow to do things.

Is there really a difference between asking Claude to generate me a SQL query that solves an island and gaps problem im dealing with versus me googling it and taking a sample from a Medium article?

comments.author: EchoLocation8
comments.body:
This is kinda the crux of the problem with vibe coders.  They can’t know what AI isn’t good at because they don’t really know what it’s doing to begin with.  And so while you can yolo Claude to a certain extent, you’ll reach a point where your inability to articulate what you need done or what is wrong leads you to running in circles.

When I use Claude, it’s basically given no creative license, because I already know exactly how what I’m building should work and how it should be designed.  It’s basically just a keyboard replacement for my old shitty fingers.  It’s the times when I have to use AI for something I don’t know how to do already that I want to blow my brains out.

Like I ask this company for guidance on doing something I haven’t done before, they tell me to use their proprietary AI Agent, I use the agent, the agent assures me everything is correct, I can’t validate that claim because idk wtf I’m doing, the feature wasn’t correct, and now I have to sit there in a dumb ass loop with this agent trying to debug wtf is wrong and I have no confidence because I’m not an expert at this company’s product.
